## A grand journey through Argentina: what to see in 15 days

This **15-day, 14-night** itinerary connects very different parts of Argentina: the capital, tropical waterfalls in the north, dry mountain gorges, wine valleys at the foot of the Andes and Patagonia's glaciers. It also includes **the Brazilian side of Iguazú Falls**, so the itinerary officially visits two countries, although most days are spent in Argentina.

Unlike a short trip combining Buenos Aires with the falls, this journey includes several overnight stays in small northwestern towns and three nights in Mendoza. It suits a couple interested in culture, natural landscapes and gastronomy who are comfortable changing hotels and taking domestic flights.

## How time is distributed between the regions

| Stage | What you will see |
| --- | --- |
| Buenos Aires | City neighborhoods and tango |
| Iguazú | Waterfalls from both sides |
| Salta and Jujuy | Mountain roads and gorges |
| Mendoza | Wineries and the Andes |
| El Calafate | Perito Moreno and the lake |
| Buenos Aires | Return and departure |

The first two nights are in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). A sightseeing day covers Plaza de Mayo, Casa Rosada, San Telmo, Recoleta and La Boca, followed by dinner at Gala Tango with private transfers. This city section includes a Russian-speaking guide and allows travelers to settle into the country before the sequence of transfers begins.

The next two nights are spent around Iguazú. On the Argentine side, travelers follow park trails toward Devil's Throat; on the Brazilian side, they enjoy panoramic views across the cascades. The distinction matters: views, walkways and border procedures differ between the two parks. Gran Meliá Iguazú is on the Argentine side, while the excursion to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) requires a border crossing from the [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) area. The visit order and entry requirements must be checked for each guest's documents.

## Northern Argentina: archaeology, mountain roads and salt flats

The five-day section following Iguazú travels through [Salta](/argentina/place/salta/), Guachipas, [Cafayate](/argentina/place/cafayate/), Cachi, [Quebrada de Humahuaca](/argentina/place/quebrada-de-humahuaca/), [Purmamarca](/argentina/place/purmamarca/) and [Salinas Grandes](/argentina/place/salinas-grandes/). Unlike Patagonia, this region is known for layered rock formations, high plateaus, settlements and historic routes.

Quebrada de Humahuaca is recognized by UNESCO as a cultural landscape used for travel and trade for thousands of years. Stops in small towns and at archaeological sites therefore have value in their own right, rather than serving merely as viewpoints.

The northern itinerary is more demanding than the map suggests: some days involve mountain drives, early departures and an overnight stay in a different town. Roads to the salt flats and high-altitude sections deserve particular attention. Guests sensitive to altitude or long vehicle journeys should discuss a suitable pace and stopping times before booking.

## Mendoza: why the itinerary includes three nights

After the northern mountains, the journey moves to [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/). Three nights are scheduled at Entre Cielos, with two excursion days divided between wine-producing areas.

**Luján de Cuyo** is known for its wineries and the history of Argentine Malbec. A separate day takes place in the **Uco Valley**, where vineyards lie against high Andean scenery. Both days include tastings and a Russian-speaking guide. Winery visits must be agreed against the itinerary, as particular producers may have date and availability restrictions.

This allows a more meaningful comparison than a single general tour: you can explore two wine regions without flying to a new city every evening. If wine interests you more than the other destinations, see the [food and wine journeys](/interests/food-and-wine/).

## Patagonia without a multi-day trek

The final nature section is based in [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/). The arrival evening includes Nativo Experience: an off-road trip beside Lake Argentino, a visit to Walichu caves with ancient imagery, and dinner inside a cave.

The following day is dedicated to [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/). The main program includes an excursion with a Russian-speaking guide, admission to Los Glaciares and **a shared-group boat safari**. This is an important detail: a private tour for two does not mean that every excursion is exclusive to those two travelers.

Standard glacier sightseeing follows established walkways and viewing platforms of varying lengths, but wind, rain and availability of the boat excursion depend on the day. A full hike on the ice is not included. Warm, wind-resistant clothing and grippy footwear are needed in the south, even if the northern days are hot.

## Hotels, guides and price

The trip is designed for **two travelers**. Specific hotels and room categories are listed for its stages: Four Seasons Buenos Aires (City View), Gran Meliá Iguazú (Deluxe), Grace Cafayate (Deluxe), Alejandro I in Salta (Premium), Mirador del Virrey in Purmamarca (Cabaña), Entre Cielos in Mendoza (Superior) and EOLO near El Calafate (Corner). The accommodation plan uses BB for bed and breakfast.

**The price starts at $12,500 net per person when traveling as a couple.** The quotation is marked net, a pricing basis that should not automatically be presented as the final retail rate for any party size. The tour description does not yet provide one consolidated list of every inclusion and exclusion. Domestic flights, additional expenses, tickets and individual service conditions are therefore confirmed when arrangements are made.

Explicitly listed elements include accommodation and breakfasts, guides on the specified days, Gala Tango with dinner, winery visits and tastings, Nativo Experience dinner, admission tickets and the group boat safari near the glacier. Guiding language and private or shared formats are checked **day by day**, rather than assumed from the trip title.

## Planning seasons and flights

Iguazú has a warm, humid climate, Argentina's northwest is strongly affected by altitude and dry air, while Patagonia can be windy with sudden weather changes. Pack light clothes, warm layers, sun protection and a windproof jacket. These climatic contrasts matter more than one forecast for “weather in Argentina.”

The route includes domestic flights between distant regions. Ada Tours helps arrange a practical sequence, connection times and actual park visiting conditions for the chosen dates. **Departure dates require separate agreement**, so flights and accommodation should be coordinated together.

## Frequently asked questions about the tour

### Is this entirely a private journey?

The core program is designed for two guests, with private transfers and the specified guides. However, the Perito Moreno boat safari is **a shared-group excursion**. Check the precise arrangement for every activity.

### Why does an Argentina tour include Brazil?

Because Iguazú Falls are visited from both sides. The Brazilian side lies across an international border and is a required stage of this itinerary.

### Is the route suitable for those avoiding difficult hikes?

No multi-day trekking is scheduled. However, the northern section includes lengthy mountain drives and some high-altitude stops. Travelers should assess the demands according to their health and prior experience at altitude.

### What does the $12,500 net price mean?

It is the stated base cost **per person for two travelers**. Additional expenses and the final calculation are confirmed for the specific dates and conditions, since no single complete list of exclusions is provided.

## Argentina in 14 days: Patagonia, Bariloche and both sides of Iguazú

This itinerary brings together several very different journeys: the neighborhoods of [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), southern Patagonia's glaciers, Tierra del Fuego's forests, Andean lakes and tropical waterfalls on the Brazilian border. It lasts **14 days and 13 nights**. The main program covers two countries, Argentina and Brazil; [Montevideo](/uruguay/) remains an optional outing from the capital, not an obligatory stop.

The tour is suitable for travelers who want to experience Argentina's geographical diversity in one trip and are ready to change cities frequently. Compared with a leisurely holiday in one region, there are more flights and short stays. This also affects the total budget: **international and domestic flights are paid separately**.

## How the stops are arranged and why their order matters

| Days | Main area |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | Buenos Aires |
| 4–5 | El Calafate |
| 6–7 | Ushuaia |
| 8–9 | Bariloche |
| 10–12 | Iguazú |
| 13–14 | Buenos Aires |

The capital opens the journey with sightseeing and a tango show with dinner. A free third day allows you to rest before the southern flights or choose an optional excursion to the Tigre Delta, a gaucho ranch or Uruguay via La Plata. All these options cost extra, and they cannot all fit into one free day.

The route continues through [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) and [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/). Each stay includes two nights, allowing major sights to be visited without multi-day hikes. After Bariloche, a connecting flight via Buenos Aires takes travelers to Iguazú. The return to the capital comes before the international flight home.

This sequence introduces several nature zones but calls for careful attention to connections, baggage allowances and time at airports. Private transfers under the itinerary are included; the domestic air tickets themselves must be budgeted separately.

## El Calafate and Perito Moreno Glacier

From El Calafate, a shared-group excursion with an English-speaking guide visits [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/). The main visit takes place at viewing platforms, overlooking the ice wall, lake and parts of the moving glacier. Blocks of ice may calve, but this cannot be scheduled for a particular hour.

The glacier is part of [Los Glaciares National Park](/argentina/place/los-glaciares-national-park/), known for the glacial landscapes of the southern Andes. Ice trekking is offered separately at $500 per person. It requires different physical effort and time on the glacier compared with a standard viewing-platform visit. Distinguish between the included excursion and this paid option.

## Ushuaia and Bariloche: two different sides of Patagonia

In [Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/), travelers explore bays, forests and coasts near Ushuaia. The included outing takes place in a group with an English-speaking guide. An excursion to [Martillo Island](/argentina/place/martillo-island/) for a walk near penguins is offered separately for $450 per person. A penguin encounter is therefore not a guaranteed part of the basic itinerary.

Around Bariloche, nature looks different: mountain lakes and wooded slopes in northern Patagonia. The Circuito Chico route introduces the city's surroundings, while a catamaran goes to Victoria Island and the [Arrayanes Forest](/argentina/place/arrayanes-forest/). Both outings are scheduled for day nine. Their order and feasibility on one day are coordinated when booking; it helps to know the assembly and return times in advance.

## Iguazú: why visit both sides of the border?

On the Argentine side, the focus is the walkways, upper and lower circuits and viewpoints at Devil's Throat. [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) is the starting point for exploring these cascades. On the Brazilian side around [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), the main excursion provides wider panoramas of the entire system. Both visits are part of the standard itinerary and are private outings led by a Russian-speaking guide.

These are two national parks across an international border. Their logistics differ, including border-crossing time and hotel location. The route names the Foz do Iguaçu region, while the accommodation list specifies Mercure Iguazu; the actual side of the border for the hotel and transfer arrangements are agreed when booking. A helicopter flight, Bird Park and water adventures are optional paid activities.

## Hotels, guides and costs: what to compare before choosing

The itinerary lists 4-star hotels and breakfasts: 474 Buenos Aires, Calafate Parque, Wyndham Garden Ushuaia, Rochester Bariloche and Mercure Iguazu. Included services comprise the main excursions and entrance tickets, scheduled transfers and a tango show with dinner. **Guiding languages vary:** private excursions in Buenos Aires and Iguazú are in Russian, while group tours in El Calafate, Ushuaia and Bariloche are in English.

The prices refer to the **2026 itinerary**. The per-person rate starts at $5,096 with triple accommodation for a party of three; for two people sharing a DBL room, it is $5,506 per person. These are different pricing bases, so comparing only the lowest amount without group size and room type is misleading. Availability and pricing for other dates require separate agreement.

When comparing this itinerary with shorter [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/), decide whether you need Ushuaia, the Bariloche lake district and two days at Iguazú together. These varied nature stops distinguish the full two-week route from a trip limited to the capital and the glacier.

## Frequently asked questions about the two-week itinerary

### Are flights between Argentine cities included?

No. Domestic and international air tickets are paid separately; transfers under the core itinerary are included. Several flights and baggage charges must be counted when estimating the total cost.

### Can we see penguins in Ushuaia?

Yes, on an optional paid excursion to Martillo Island. The standard day features Tierra del Fuego National Park, and the penguin encounter is not automatically included.

### Is Uruguay a required stop?

No. Montevideo is mentioned as an optional excursion from Buenos Aires. The main countries of the itinerary are Argentina and Brazil.

### Is the itinerary suitable without speaking English?

Some excursions have Russian-speaking guides, while the group visits in El Calafate, Ushuaia and Bariloche are in English. Russian-language guiding may be available for an extra fee on some stages and must be arranged separately.

## Argentina and Brazil in 10 days: from Buenos Aires and the glacier to Rio

This itinerary lasts **10 days and 9 nights**. First, you explore [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), then fly to [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) to see [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/). Next are Iguazú Falls on both sides of the border, before three nights in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) conclude the journey.

The program suits travelers who want to combine city experiences, icy Patagonia and tropical scenery in one holiday. That variety comes with several domestic flights and marked changes in weather. If you prefer fewer transfers, consider the [9-day Rio – Iguazú – Buenos Aires itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-rio-iguazu-buenos-aires-9-days/) without Patagonia.

## How nights and experiences are distributed

| Stop | What is planned |
|---|---|
| Buenos Aires, 2 nights | City tour and neighborhoods |
| El Calafate, 2 nights | Perito Moreno and viewpoints |
| Iguazú, 2 nights | Argentine and Brazilian sides |
| Rio, 3 nights | Sugarloaf, Corcovado, city center |

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), sightseeing combines central squares and avenues with La Boca, San Telmo, Palermo and Recoleta. La Boca is known for its port history and colorful houses, while San Telmo offers historic architecture and tango traditions. The itinerary also contains a separate tango excursion module; consult the tour page for its precise contents.

The route then heads south. From El Calafate, a **shared-group excursion to Perito Moreno with an English-speaking guide** is scheduled. From the viewing walkways, visitors can see blue crevasses and the ice wall from several angles. Walking on the glacier itself is not listed among this program's inclusions: viewing it from established platforms and ice trekking are different activities.

## Iguazú: why both sides of the border matter

From [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), walkways approach individual cascades. The viewing routes show the falls from above and from the side. On the [Brazilian side near Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), visitors enjoy a broad panorama, making it easier to appreciate the entire waterfall system.

The tour therefore provides separate excursion days for Argentina and Brazil. **Crossing the international border** and passport-specific entry requirements must be taken into account. During major floods, some Argentine walkways may close for safety, so access to individual viewpoints, particularly Devil's Throat, must be checked immediately before visiting.

After Iguazú, the journey continues to Rio. [Sugarloaf Mountain](/brazil/place/sugarloaf-mountain/) provides views across the city and Guanabara Bay from one direction, while Corcovado offers another perspective over wooded hills and the urban landscape. The historic neighborhoods of central Rio are also included.

## Allowing enough time to travel between regions

On paper, the journey looks compact, but flights between Buenos Aires, El Calafate, Iguazú and Rio consume substantial parts of several days. When changing cities, transport and hotel check-in become the principal activities. Schedule any additional multi-hour excursion on the same day only after checking actual flight times.

The climate also changes abruptly. Patagonia requires warm layers and protection from wind and precipitation, while Iguazú calls for light clothes, comfortable shoes and waterproof protection against spray. Los Glaciares National Park's administration advises preparing for changeable weather and wearing appropriate shoes on grated viewing walkways. Light clothing and sun protection are sensible for Rio.

## Price, guides and separately paid services

**The program costs $3,230 per person** with DBL accommodation in 3-star hotels and a group of two people, as specified in the tour terms. Included are accommodation, scheduled excursions and transfers, private Russian-speaking sightseeing in Buenos Aires, Iguazú and Rio, and a shared-group English-language excursion in El Calafate.

**Domestic flights between the four stops are excluded.** International flights, optional excursions, and food and drinks during transfers also cost extra. Your total travel expenditure will therefore exceed the land-program price. Pay particular attention to the connection between Patagonia and Iguazú; compare the full air route, not just the guided-tour package.

## Choosing between similar itineraries

Compare the exact sights, number of nights, guiding languages and flight inclusions. Two tours with similar country names can differ considerably in costs and the number of transfers.

## Frequently asked questions about the 10-day tour

### Can I see Perito Moreno Glacier without special equipment?

Yes. This itinerary includes an excursion using viewpoints near the glacier. Walking on the ice is not necessary to experience Perito Moreno; separate ice trekking is not included in the base package.

### Is only one side of Iguazú included?

No. The itinerary visits both the Argentine and Brazilian sides on separate days. Access to any particular park or viewing route depends on the actual operating conditions on the day.

### Will I have a Russian-speaking guide everywhere?

No. Russian-language guiding is included in Buenos Aires, Iguazú and Rio. El Calafate has a shared-group excursion with an English-speaking guide.

### Are flights included in the $3,230?

No. Domestic and international flights are paid separately; the figure is for the land program under the agreed accommodation and group conditions.

## Argentina and Patagonia in 26 days: from Buenos Aires to Tierra del Fuego

This itinerary lasts **26 days and 25 nights** and covers four countries: **Argentina, Uruguay, Brazil and Chile**. Most of the journey is in Argentina, but the program deliberately includes visits beyond its borders. From [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), travelers visit [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/); the [Iguazú](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) natural complex is explored from both sides, and a Patagonia day is dedicated to Chile's [Torres del Paine region](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/).

Within Argentina, the journey passes through strikingly different regions: the northwest with multicolored mountains and salt flats, Mendoza's wine country, Bariloche's lakes, southern Patagonia's glaciers and mountain trails, and finally Tierra del Fuego. **It is designed for travelers who want a broad introduction to the country in one trip**, rather than just Buenos Aires and the waterfalls.

## The first six days: Buenos Aires, Uruguay and both sides of Iguazú

Days 1–2 focus on [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), its architecture, historic neighborhoods and capital-city culture. Day three includes a ferry journey to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and back. **Uruguay is thus a day visit**, not a separate multi-day tour of the country.

On day four, the journey continues into Brazil around [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). Day five explores the Brazilian side of the falls; day six covers the [Argentine side near Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). These visits complement each other: Brazil offers broad panoramas of the cascades, while Argentine walkways bring visitors closer to individual parts of the waterfall system.

The two Iguazú national parks are separately listed by UNESCO as World Heritage protected areas. Visiting both sides **requires accounting for border crossings and document rules** according to nationality. The availability of particular walkways depends on park conditions.

## The northwest: Salta, Cafayate and salt flats

Day seven leads via [Salta](/argentina/place/salta/) to [Cafayate](/argentina/). In subsequent days, the program covers [Los Cardones National Park](/argentina/), [Purmamarca](/argentina/place/purmamarca/) and [Salinas Grandes](/argentina/place/salinas-grandes/). Travelers encounter Andean valleys, striking landforms and high-altitude salt plains.

This scenery is very different from Iguazú's humid subtropics. The northwest calls for attention to altitude changes, cool mountain nights and strong sunlight. Anyone sensitive to altitude should discuss appropriate exertion and stopping times before arranging the journey.

Day eleven is for flying or traveling to [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/), beginning the winery section. Days twelve and thirteen visit Luján de Cuyo and the Uco Valley for vineyards and Argentine wine culture. The specific tastings and gastronomy included should be checked against the list of scheduled visits; not every winery offering can be assumed to be part of one package price.

## Bariloche: lakes, mountains and forests

On day fourteen, the journey reaches [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/). This is the lake region of Patagonia, with Victoria Island, forests, the shores of Lake Nahuel Huapi and mountain scenery. The following days include the Circuito Grande route and the Cerro Campanario area.

The Bariloche area differs from the glacial landscapes of southern Patagonia, visited later. Here the emphasis is on lakes, forested slopes and small towns; farther south, it shifts to glaciers and mountain valleys.

## El Calafate, El Chaltén and Torres del Paine

Day seventeen brings the group to [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), with [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) scheduled for day eighteen. The glacier belongs to Los Glaciares National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Viewing platforms and enormous ice formations provide the main experiences, but no one can schedule a particular block of ice to break away.

Days 19–21 are devoted to [El Chaltén](/argentina/place/el-chalten/), with mountain routes and time amid Patagonia's landscapes. **Optional kayaking starts at $300 per person**. It is excluded from the main package and is not an obligatory activity on each of those days.

On day 22, travelers visit **Chile's Torres del Paine National Park**. Chile's entry rules and current restrictions on nature trails must be checked separately. Describing the entire itinerary as Argentina-only would be inaccurate: Brazil, Uruguay and Chile are real parts of the program.

## Ushuaia: the final four days on Tierra del Fuego

Days 23–26 are based around [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/). They include a 4×4 outing to the lakes, [Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/) and the return to Buenos Aires. The climate and coast here differ sharply from the opening days.

The itinerary separately offers **an optional penguin walk for $350 per person**. This costs extra. Wild bird sightings depend on season and visiting conditions, and the outing itself may have restrictions, so it should not be considered a guaranteed inclusion.

| Days | Region |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | Buenos Aires and Montevideo |
| 4–6 | Iguazú: Brazil and Argentina |
| 7–10 | Salta, Cafayate, Purmamarca |
| 11–13 | Mendoza and wineries |
| 14–16 | Bariloche's lake district |
| 17–22 | El Calafate, El Chaltén, Chile |
| 23–26 | Ushuaia and return |

## Price, flights and travel arrangements

The journey costs **USD 13,707 per person for two participants**. It includes hotel accommodation, specified meals, guided excursions on the indicated days, transfers with a driver and the ferry between Buenos Aires and Montevideo. The Buenos Aires city tour and Argentine side of Iguazú use a Russian-speaking guide; other outings include English-speaking guides.

**Domestic and international flights are paid separately.** This is especially significant on a 26-day itinerary with many flights between distant regions. Optional excursions, meals and drinks outside the included services, tips and laundry are also excluded.

The price refers to the **2027 itinerary**. When planning, dates, hotels, flights and entry arrangements for all four countries must be agreed while preserving the stated structure of the trip.

## Who should choose the extended itinerary?

This journey is for those who want to explore Argentina from north to south and add neighboring countries without having to organize dozens of transfers independently. Those interested in [nature and wildlife](/interests/wildlife/) will find waterfalls, glaciers and national parks; [culture and history](/interests/culture-and-history/) enthusiasts will find capitals and regional heritage. The wine section is particularly attractive to those who enjoy [food and wine travel](/interests/food-and-wine/).

Both shorter options cover Buenos Aires, southern Patagonia and Iguazú, but omit the northwest, Mendoza, Bariloche and the separate visit to Chile.

## Frequently asked questions about the 26-day journey

### Which countries are included?

Argentina, Uruguay, Brazil and Chile. The main multi-day sections are in Argentina; the Montevideo excursion, Brazilian Iguazú visit and Torres del Paine outing are separate stages.

### Are domestic flights included?

No. Both domestic and international flights are listed among costs outside the base price.

### Is there enough time for Mendoza and Patagonia?

Several days of winery visits are planned in Mendoza; the south has separate stages for El Calafate, El Chaltén, Torres del Paine and Ushuaia. Actual walking time depends on the daily itinerary and transfers.

### Are penguins and kayaking included in the price?

No. The published description lists the penguin walk and El Chaltén kayaking as optional paid activities.

## Brazil, Argentina and Chile in 13 days: how the extended route works

This tour connects three very different parts of South America. It begins in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), by the ocean and the city's major landmarks, before reaching Iguazú Falls on the Brazil–Argentina border. After [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), the route heads south toward [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) and Chile's [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), then ends in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and the Atacama Desert.

Over **13 days and 12 nights**, travelers take several domestic flights, cross a land border in Patagonia and spend a high-altitude day above 4,000 meters. The central consideration is therefore a readiness for frequent changes of city and natural environment. This is a sightseeing itinerary with excursions, not a multi-day sporting trek.

## How the days are divided

| Days | Main region |
| --- | --- |
| 1–2 | Rio de Janeiro |
| 3–4 | Iguazú and Buenos Aires |
| 5–6 | Buenos Aires, Perito Moreno |
| 7–8 | Chilean Patagonia |
| 9–11 | Santiago, Atacama |
| 12–13 | Santiago, Maipo Valley |

The sequence shows which stages require flights and where the route runs overland. Especially busy are the transitions from Iguazú to Buenos Aires, onward to El Calafate, and after Patagonia to central and northern Chile. No extended stay at one resort is scheduled.

## Rio and both sides of Iguazú: why they belong together

In Rio, sightseeing days include [Corcovado with Christ the Redeemer](/brazil/place/corcovado-christ-the-redeemer/) and [Sugarloaf Mountain](/brazil/place/sugarloaf-mountain/). Their viewpoints introduce the city's geography: bays, beaches and wooded hills. A flight then takes travelers to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/).

Day three visits the Brazilian side of the falls, day four the Argentine side near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). These offer different perspectives: Brazil presents the broad width of the cascades, while Argentine walkways take visitors closer to individual streams. Both national parks protect parts of one waterfall system and its subtropical forest.

The Brazilian stage includes Macuco Safari and the Bird Park, while a helicopter flight is optional. Waterproof protection is useful on the boat and viewing walkways. Access to particular paths depends on river conditions and park rules.

## Argentina: from tango to Patagonia's ice

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), the program includes a tour of historic neighborhoods and an evening tango show with dinner. This is a city stop between intensive nature excursions. The next flight takes travelers to [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/).

The main attraction of Argentine Patagonia is [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) in [Los Glaciares National Park](/argentina/place/los-glaciares-national-park/). Its ice face is visible from viewing walkways, with Lake Argentino and mountains framing the glacial valley. Ice may break off, but the time cannot be predicted.

The following day involves an overland transfer from Argentina to Chile, toward Puerto Natales. Border-crossing procedures and travel time are arranged in advance; schedules depend on the travelers' documents, road conditions and weather.

## Torres del Paine and Atacama: two very different parts of Chile

The [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) excursion offers views of the park, Pehoé and Grey lakes and the glacier area. This is a day visit from Puerto Natales. The W and O circuits are separate possibilities in the region, but completing these multi-day treks **is not part of this itinerary**.

The journey then continues via Santiago to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). A desert day includes an astronomy program and [Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/), where salt formations, dunes and rock surfaces change color in the evening light. The next excursion visits high-altitude lagoons above **4,000 meters**, calling for special attention to altitude and physical well-being.

The closing stages include a city tour of Santiago and a visit with tasting to vineyards in the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/). The tour ends more quietly than the glacier and transfer days.

## Clothing and preparation

One suitcase must work for Iguazú's humid warmth, windy Patagonia and the cold highlands. At the waterfalls, light quick-drying clothes and waterproof document protection are useful. For Patagonia's parks, bring closed shoes, a warm layer and a windproof jacket. In Atacama, sun protection, drinking water and warm evening clothes are particularly important.

**The high-altitude lagoons** are a separate consideration when choosing this tour. Travelers with medical conditions that may be affected by altitude should discuss this day with their doctor and the organizer before booking. Entry, transit and land-border rules must be checked according to nationality and current documentation, not assumed from the tour name.

## Frequently asked questions about the Brazil, Argentina and Chile tour

### Does the itinerary include both sides of Iguazú?

Yes. The Brazilian side is scheduled on day three and the Argentine side on day four. These are separate visits to the same natural complex.

### Are domestic air tickets included?

No. The conditions specify domestic flights paid separately, from USD 1,500 per person on top of the base tour rate.

### Do I need to complete a multi-day trek in Patagonia?

No. Perito Moreno Glacier and a day excursion to Torres del Paine are included. The full W and O circuits are not compulsory activities.

### What requires special preparation?

Frequent transfers, contrasting weather and the excursion to lagoons above 4,000 meters. Assess altitude tolerance in advance and bring clothing for several climate zones.
